#### **<u>Highlights</u>** 

###### **Chinese copper consumption likely to rebound on policy support, but when?** 

To maintain economic momentum and expand domestic demand, as well as boost economic restructuring and energy savings, China’s government carried out a series of incentive policies. On May 16, the State Council announced that the government will earmark 26.5 billion yuan (US$4.2 billion) to subsidize the consumption of household electrical appliances for one-year period. The appliances include air conditioners, flat-panel television sets, refrigerators, washing machines and water heaters that meet energy-saving standards. Meanwhile, the government will allocate another 2.2 billion yuan (US$355 million yuan) t

o promote the consumption of energy-saving light bulbs and LEDs (light-emitting diodes) and 6 billion yuan (US$968 million yuan) for purchases of vehicles with engine sizes below 1.6 liters. Another 1.6 billion yuan (US$258 million yuan) will be earmarked to promote the consumption of highly efficient electrical machinery, which did not elaborate on how the subsidies will be implemented. It is expected that new subsidies will induce domestic consumption totaling 450 billion yuan (US$71 billion). One salesman from Suning Appliance Co., Ltd., one of the largest privately owned electrical appliance retailers in China, showed that the subsidies policy for energy-saving appliances made less effect than previous subsidies policies, like Home Appliance Replacement Scheme and China's Home Appliance Subsidy Program for Rural Areas, due to small market share of energy-saving appliances in Chinese home appliances market. 

On July 5, the People's Bank of China lowered the benchmark deposit rates by 25 basis points and cut lending rates by 31 basis points, the second time in a month. Interest cut will strengthen expectations for warming housing market, but its direct effects are limited and significant price rebounds are unlikely, according to Chen Guoqiang, Vice chairman of China Real Estate Society (CRES) 

Under current situation, financial feature of copper has more and more influence on copper prices. It can't be denied that loosening monetary policy will give good support for copper prices. But it is difficult for the single policy to spur copper prices rising. Firstly, without other supporting polices, stimulation of the loosening monetary policy can’t be turned into real downstream demand in a short term. Secondly, worldwide downside risks remain significant as the debt crises in the Eurozone and the US are likely to deteriorate in the coming months. Currently, copper prices have expectations to rise but lack of adequate driving force. It is estimated that copper consumption will be getting better in the third quarter of 2012 under the comprehensive function of Chinese loosening monetary policies and a new round of stimulus measures.

#### **Copper Market Commentary** 

###### **Copper price review in H1 2012** 

Copper prices showed a trend of first rally and then fall back, hitting the highest level of USD8,765/t on Feb. 9 of 2012. After that, copper prices began to fall in Apr. due to lack of rising power and facing uncertainties from macro economy environment. Copper prices continued the trend of unilateral downward and continuously fell below several support lines in May. Copper prices maintained weak shock in June, hitting lowest level in the year at USD7,220/t. 

In H1 2012, average copper price of LME cash month and 3-month reached USD8,087/t and USD8,069/t, down by 13.98% and 14.22% YoY, down by 1.85% and 2.32% compared with H2 2011, respectively. 

Copper prices o

n SHFE were weak than LME. In H1 2012, average prices of SHFE cash month copper and 3-month copper reached 57,830yuan/t and 57,800yuan/t, down by 17.90% and 17.85% YoY, down by 6.09% and 5.49% compared with H2 2011, respectively. On the whole, in the first half of 2012, global macro economy environment was not good, especially Europe Zone debt crisis made metal goods market under great pressure. But copper prices got relative good support in view of good fundamentals and strong financial features, as well as continuously high level of Chinese copper import. In recent years, domestic copper inventory in bonded warehouse maintained at a high level. It is estimated that current copper stock is 500kt or over and most of them are financing copper. Copper import in the form of financing copper will keep active because financing action will likely to be an effective way of easing financial pressure for some investors. So high level of Chinese copper stock will continues exist in Chinese copper market. According Antaike’s statistics, output of domestic 12 major refined copper producers reached 1.63Mt during Jan to May, up by 4.34% YoY. Of them, output of Jiangxi Copper, Tongling Nonferrous, Jinchuang Group and Yunnan Copper accounted for about 77% of the total. Domestic refined copper output growth are mainly driven by domestic expanding refining/smelting capacity. Refined copper output from scraps reached 691kt during Jan to May, up by 12.4% YoY, accounting for about 34% of refined c

opper output. 

CNIA data still showed that copper semis production was 4.33Mt during Jan to May, up by 9.8% YoY, a great down compared with year on year rise of 17.95% in the same period of 2011, although which has always been larger than Antaike’s statistics. But this official data signaled that domestic copper consumption growth has been greatly slowed down but not pessimistic.

###### **Chinese refined copper imports and exports both rise in May** 

Statistics released by China’s Customs showed that Chinese refined copper import amounted to 1.63Mt during Jan to May, up by 80.2% YoY, most of which were financing actions. Refined copper export reached 102kt in May, hitting a history record, with year-on-year rise of 407.4% and month-on-month rise of 273.4%. During Jan to May, Chinese refined copper export amounted to 157kt, up by 9.17% YoY, close to the total export volume in 2011. It is estimated that refined copper export will drop in June, but export volume will be more than 50kt, due to such as factors as previous export formalities and sailing date, plus entrepot trade going on. Antaike estimates that Chinese refined copper export will be slowed down until normal level in Q3. 

Copper concentrate import reached 668kt in May, up by 10.7% MoM and 43.6% YoY. Copper scraps import was 424kt in May, up by 14.3% MoM and 6.3% YoY. During Jan to May, copper scraps import reached 1.86Mt, up by 4.6% YoY, roughly equal to the level compared with the same period of 2011 based on metal content because metal content in imported copper scraps this year is lower than last year. In consideration of expanding copper semis capacity and no obvious rise of Chinese copper scraps imports, domestic copper scraps supply was still in shortage.

###### **Copper consumption** 

According to data from the NBS, year-on-year growth rate of domestic copper-using products output fell during Jan to May. Refined copper consumption in major copper-using industries, like power industry and air conditioning and refrigeration industry, were weaker than expectations. Growth rate of air conditioner output declined to 2.4% during Jan to May of 2012 from 40% in the same period of 2011. 

During Jan to May, investment in domestic real estate development was 2.22 trillion yuan, up by 18.5% YoY, 0.2 percentage points lower than that in Jan to Apr. Among them, investment in residential houses was 1.51 trillion yuan, up by 13.6% YoY, 0.3 percentage points lower than that in Jan to Apr. Investment in residential houses accounted for 68.0% of the total investment. During Jan to May, floor space under construction was 4,513.64 mln sq.m, up by 19.6% YoY, 1.6 percentage points lower than that in Jan to Apr. Of them, floor space under construction of residential houses was 3,390.36 mln sq.m, at a

Completion floor space of houses was 273.06 mln sq.m, up by 26.3% YoY, 3.9 percentage points lower than that in Jan to Apr, of which completion floor space of residential houses was 218.15 mln sq.m, up by 26.5% YoY. On the whole, obvious growth slowdown in real estate industry gave a certain pressure on copper consumption. Smoothly construction of indemnificatory apartments will come to be a compensation for copper consumption at a certain degree. Investment in power generation decreased by down by 1.96% YoY, but investment portion in clean energies rises. According to statistics from China Electricity Council, completed investment in national power construction was 244.6 billion yuan, up by 1.21% YoY. Among them, investment in power generation and power grid reached 114.3 billion yuan and 100.3 billion yuan, down by 1.96% or up by 5.08% YoY, respectively. Of investment in power generation, investment in thermal power was 29.5 billion yuan, down by 25.26% YoY, lasting the down trend since 2011; investment in hydropower reached 44.4 billion yuan, up by 45.5% YoY. Besides, investment in nuclear power and wind power were 25.4 billion yuan and 14.3 billion yuan, down by 1.6% and 24.9% YoY, respectively. Investment in thermal power accounted for 25.85% of the total investment in power generation, 8.1 percentage points lower than the same period of 2011; investment in thermal power, nuclear power and wind power accounted for 73.6%, representing an obviously rise. tion growth will slow down, refined copper production will increase steadily, and Chinese net import of refined copper will continue its high level because there are financing copper demand and investment and speculative demand. All above factors will finally lead to refined copper supply surplus, and this is no exception in H1 2012. In H1 2012, domestic refined copper supply will reach 4.32Mt, up by 25.65% YoY; refined copper consumption will rise by 3.59%, at 3.75Mt, with growth rate 3 percentage points lower than that in H1 2011. So, refined copper supply will be in great surplus in H1 2012, with surplus supply of 570kt. But this kind of surplus is only reflected in the numbers, not in spot market, because a large number of refined copper are imported for financing and won’t flow into spot market and consumption field. **The Supply/Demand Balance for Refined Copper** |
